summary: Source-anchored research for defaultMaxTimeMS cluster-level read timeout. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The MongoDB server implementation README says defaultMaxTimeMS takes effect only when authentication is enabled. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Because the implementation README assigns defaultMaxTimeMS the same semantics as maxTimeMS, interpret it as a server processing-time budget: termination occurs at designated interrupt points, client-to-server network latency is excluded, and mongos-to-mongod latency is included. (medium confidence)

Configure a five-second default on the admin database with db.adminCommand({setClusterParameter:{defaultMaxTimeMS:{readOperations:5000}}}); inspect it with db.adminCommand({getClusterParameter:"defaultMaxTimeMS"}). (low confidence)
MongoDB 8.0 introduced defaultMaxTimeMS.readOperations as a cluster-wide fallback time limit in milliseconds for individual read operations that omit maxTimeMS. (high confidence)

defaultMaxTimeMS.readOperations defaults to 0, which supplies no default query timeout. It is not automatically a finite execution limit merely because the deployment uses MongoDB 8.0. (high confidence)

Atlas describes this timeout as a last-round mitigation that cancels overlong operations and limits resource retention; Tencent likewise identifies resource exhaustion prevention as its purpose. This is execution-time protection rather than a prediction that a query will be expensive. (medium confidence)

The implementation README says users with bypassDefaultMaxTimeMS ignore the default, and root and __system have that privilege by default. Verify enforcement with the application identity rather than only an administrative identity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

MongoDB Atlas documents defaultMaxTimeMS as mitigation for expensive queries, including collection scans from missing indexes; database teams can set the fallback centrally rather than rely on every application to set a timeout. Mydbops independently describes the same operational use. (medium confidence)

Supported reads are find, count, distinct, dbHash, and aggregate without $out or $merge. Aggregations containing either write stage do not inherit this default, although an explicit maxTimeMS can still apply. (high confidence)

An explicit operation-level maxTimeMS overrides the cluster default, including a longer timeout for legitimate analytics work; the setting therefore is not a mandatory upper bound on every read. (high confidence)

The MongoDB server implementation README says defaultMaxTimeMS has an effect only with authentication enabled. Users granted bypassDefaultMaxTimeMS ignore the default; root and __system include that privilege by default. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

DRIVERS-3474 reports that timeoutMS=0 in a mongosh URI does not override defaultMaxTimeMS, whereas explicit maxTimeMS(0) does. Its July 22, 2026 update describes the Node.js driver's infinite client timeout as not emitting a server maxTimeMS override and leaves the spec change unresolved. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-22)

Crossplane's provider-mongodbatlas v1.6.0 API, published October 22, 2026, exposes optional DefaultMaxTimeMs with JSON name defaultMaxTimeMs and Terraform name default_max_time_ms, showing a declarative configuration surface for the setting. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

The implementation README says commands exceeding defaultMaxTimeMS return MaxTimeMSExpired. This is an execution timeout, not a guarantee that the operation is rejected before execution begins. (low confidence)
